title: Ferromagnetic Order of Reduced Magnetic Moments in a Frustrated Sawtooth Chain of the Magnetic Semiconductor ZnYb$_2$S$_4$
authors: Shinji Okada, Hiroto Suzuki, Nonoka Higa, Yasuyuki Shimura, Takanori Taniguchi, Takahiro Onimaru
abstract: In a sawtooth spin chain, competing nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor interactions suppress long-range order, yielding novel quantum states such as a spin-dimer singlet, 1/2 magnetization plateau, and spin contraction. Here, we investigate the magnetic properties of the orthorhombic semiconductor ZnYb$_2$S$_4$, in which Yb$^{3+}$ ions with an effective spin-1/2 form a sawtooth chain along the $b$-axis. The specific heat exhibits a sharp peak at ${T}_{\rm m}$ $=$ 1.4 K, at which the magnetic entropy $S_{\rm m}$ reaches only 27% of $R$ln2. This reduced $S_{\rm m}$ at $T_{\rm m}$ indicates the entropy release of the ground state doublet of Yb$^{3+}$ even for $T$ $>$ $T_{\rm m}$. The isothermal magnetization $M(B)$ at 0.28 K exhibits hysteresis for $\left|B\right| \leq 0.2$ T and increases monotonically for $B > 0.2$ T. The spontaneous magnetization is only 0.1 ${\it μ}_{\rm B}$$/$Yb, an order of magnitude smaller than that expected for the ground state doublet of Yb$^{3+}$. Moreover, in powder neutron diffraction measurements, no superlattice reflections due to antiferromagnetic order are observed for $T$ $<$ $T_{\rm m}$. Therefore, in the ground state, the Yb moments are ferromagnetically aligned, but their amplitude is reduced by magnetic frustration in the sawtooth Yb chain.
summary: The study investigates $	ext{ZnYb}_2	ext{S}_4$, a material featuring Yb ions arranged in a frustrated sawtooth chain. Through detailed measurements of specific heat and magnetization, the authors demonstrate that magnetic frustration suppresses the expected long-range antiferromagnetic order below $T_m = 1.4 	ext{ K}$. The results suggest the ground state features ferromagnetically aligned but significantly reduced moments.
main_problem: Investigating how magnetic frustration within a sawtooth chain structure affects the ground state magnetic order of $	ext{Yb}^{3+}$ moments in the semiconductor $	ext{ZnYb}_2	ext{S}_4$.
main_result: The system exhibits evidence of magnetic frustration, leading to reduced spontaneous magnetization despite underlying antiferromagnetic correlations; the ground state is characterized by ferromagnetically aligned but suppressed Yb moments.
method: A combination of bulk measurements including specific heat ($C(T)$), isothermal magnetization ($M(B)$), and powder neutron diffraction were employed.
model_or_system: The physical system is the orthorhombic semiconductor $	ext{ZnYb}_2	ext{S}_4$, where $	ext{Yb}^{3+}$ ions form a sawtooth spin chain along the $b$-axis, modeled by competing nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor exchange interactions.
key_observables: Specific heat peak at $T_m = 1.4 	ext{ K}$, magnetic entropy release ($27\%$ of $R\ln2$ at $T_m$), hysteresis in $M(B)$, and absence of superlattice reflections in neutron diffraction.
important_parameters: $T_m = 1.4 	ext{ K}$ (transition temperature); $	heta_p < 0$ (indicating AFM interactions); spontaneous magnetization $\approx 0.1 \mu_B/	ext{Yb}$.
main_assumptions: The magnetic behavior is governed by the effective spin-1/2 Kramers doublet ground state derived from Crystal Electric Field theory.
figures_summary: Figures show $C(T)$ peaks, $M(B)$ hysteresis loops, and neutron diffraction patterns confirming the nature of the magnetic ordering below $T_m$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using a sawtooth chain Hamiltonian and CEF analysis. It then presents experimental results from specific heat and magnetization measurements to identify the transition temperature ($T_m$) and quantify frustration via entropy release. Finally, neutron diffraction confirms the nature of the magnetic order.
why_interesting: This work provides an excellent example of how geometric frustration in a low-dimensional quantum magnet can suppress expected long-range order, leading to novel ground states that are sensitive to external fields.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (Color online) (a) One-dimensional spin chain with nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor exchange interactions, J1 (blue) and J2 (red). Note that J2 acts on every other site. (b) A sawtooth spin chain with J1 and J2 equivalent to the one-dimensional model. (c) Orthorhombic crystal structure of ZnYb2S4 with the space group of Pnma. There are two Yb3+ sites, which are labeled Yb(1) at the 4a site (¯1) and Yb(2) at the 4c site (m). (d) The Yb3+ ions of Yb(1) and Yb(2) form a sawtooth chain along the b-axis.

FIG. 2. (Color online) Temperature dependence of the magnetic susceptibility M(T )/B of ZnYb2S4 measured in B = 0.1 T (left-hand scale), and the inverse susceptibility B/M (right-hand scale). The broken line indicates a Curie– Weiss ﬁt, and the solid (blue) line is a calculation considering the CEF eﬀect for a Yb3+ ion. The inset presents the temper- ature dependence of the magnetization in B = 0.03, 0.1, and 0.5 T. Tm denotes the magnetic ordering temperature. The right inset shows the Yb(1) site encapsulated in a slightly dis- torted S octahedron.

FIG. 3. (Color online) Temperature dependence of the mag- netic speciﬁc heat divided by temperature, Cm/T (left-hand scale), and the magnetic entropy, Sm (right-hand scale), of ZnYb2S4. Tm denotes the magnetic ordering temperature, and T ∗indicates an extrinsic anomaly due to an impurity phase. The inset shows the temperature dependence of the speciﬁc heat, C(T ). The solid line represents the phonon contribution estimated using a Debye model. See the text in detail.

FIG. 4. (Color online) Temperature dependence of the spe- ciﬁc heat C of ZnYb2S4 in B = 0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 1, and 3 T. The inset shows the B–T phase diagram. PM denotes the para- magnetic phase, and the broken line indicates the crossover. The illustration indicates that the reduced Yb moments (red arrows) on the sawtooth chain are developed (blue arrows) due to release of the magnetic frustration with the applica- tion of magnetic ﬁelds.
